subject: POC next steps, success criteria & final readout scheduling - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Torres <jill@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-10T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: POC next steps & success criteria - Acme Health

Hi Jill — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned ahead of the trial:

1) Agreed success criteria (please confirm):
   - Retrieval + reranking: top-1 answer accuracy >= 92% on your sampled evaluation set
   - Generation latency: p95 <= 600ms (single region)
   - Throughput: sustain 50 qps with <= 10% degradation under load for 1 hour
   - Data handling: logs stored for 30 days, PII redaction enabled for PHI-sensitive fields

2) Evaluation plan & timeline:
   - Trial period: 2 weeks (proposed 2027-02-14 -> 2027-02-25)
   - Redwood to provision a scoped environment and ingest sample index (Marcus)
   - Acme to provide evaluation queries and the labeled eval set (Jill/Adam)
   - Weekly syncs: kickoff (w/ tech leads), mid-trial check-in, final readout with execs

3) Owners:
   - Redwood: Marcus (tech provisioning), Neha (security/compliance), me (POC lead & readout)
   - Acme: Adam (tech), Jill (product), procurement contact for contracting

4) Next immediate asks: please confirm the success criteria above and whether the 2-week window looks good on your side. I've attached the POC plan (ACME_POC_Plan_v1.docx) and a short checklist.

Proposed final readout: week of Feb 24 — our preference is Feb 25, 11:00am ET (we can flex). The readout will include performance readouts, live demo, and a short pricing/next-steps section for exec decision.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachment: ACME_POC_Plan_v1.docx (POC plan, owners, timeline)

From: Jill Torres <jill@acme-health.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: POC next steps & success criteria - Acme Health

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming most of the success criteria; two small notes:

- Can we relax throughput target during the trial to sustain 40 qps (our production baseline) instead of 50 qps? We can stress test separately.
- For latency, p95 <= 600ms is fine if we measure excluding network overhead (i.e., service-side).

Timeline works for us — Feb 14–25 is good. Final readout: Feb 25 at 11:00am ET works for the execs (I'll invite Adam Reyes, our CTO, and our Head of Data).

Procurement note: we'll likely need SOC 2 evidence and a clean pricing sheet ahead of exec review; procurement timeline target is end of next week. I've attached a short note with our internal stakeholders.

Attaching: ACME_POCCriteria_v2.docx

Cheers,
Jill
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Health
jill@acme-health.com

Marcus / Neha — forwarding Jill's confirmations. Quick internal plan and asks so we don't drop the ball:

- Provisioning: Marcus, can you stand up a scoped environment (single-region) with 3 inference nodes and the retrieval index by Feb 14? We'll need an endpoint with api key for Acme test traffic.
- Monitoring: include token-level latency dashboards, p95 metrics, and cost estimate for trial duration (send a one-pager pricing-sheet-v1.xlsx).
- Security: Neha, please prepare the SOC2 summary and the standard evidence bundle (SOC2_summary.pdf) and share with Jill/procurement by EOD Feb 14.
- Eval: I'll collect the eval queries and set up the shared Google Doc to capture results and notes (see link).

I attached a short checklist for the trial. Marcus — can you confirm provisioning ETA and any quota or capacity caveats?

Thanks — Marissa

Attachment: POC_Checklist_Quick.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-11T12:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: POC next steps & success criteria - Acme Health

Confirming ETA: I can have the scoped environment provisioned and an endpoint ready by 2027-02-14 09:00 PT. I'll allocate the equivalent of 3 gpus (shared) for the two-week trial and will surface any throttling policies.

I'll also prepare a sample query set and a short evaluation rubric (precision @1, latency p95, failure rate). Pricing note: the trial cost estimate (infrastructure only) is ~USD 1,800 for the trial window — I'll include that in the pricing-sheet-v1.xlsx and drop it in the shared folder.

Related: HubSpot deal HS-18273 — I'll add notes about provisioning and expected costs.

—Marcus
